Title: Scalable SQL and NoSQL Data Stores
Problem addressed: Emergence of non-relational distributed databases and scalability limits of traditional RDBMS
Method: Qualitative comparative analysis of cloud serving stores
Key result: Formalized initial architectural classification of Key-Value, Document, and Extensible Stores
Limitation / gap: Pre-dates modern binary JSONB and multi-model database engines

Title: Benchmarking Cloud Serving Systems with YCSB
Problem addressed: Lack of standardized benchmarking frameworks for emerging NoSQL data stores
Method: Developed extensible Yahoo! Cloud Serving Benchmark (YCSB)
Key result: Established defacto benchmark standard for NoSQL latency and throughput evaluation
Limitation / gap: Evaluates only flat key-value pairs; ignores nested semi-structured JSON documents

Title: Consistency Tradeoffs in Modern Distributed Database System Design: CAP is only part of the story
Problem addressed: Inadequacy of CAP theorem to describe normal-state non-partitioned latency trade-offs
Method: Formal distributed systems analysis and PACELC formulation
Key result: Proved that latency-consistency trade-offs persist in non-partitioned normal execution states
Limitation / gap: Pure theoretical model lacking fine-grained empirical tail-latency quantification

Title: The SQL++ Query Language: Configurable, Unifying, and Computable Semi-Structured Data
Problem addressed: Incompatibility between relational SQL and nested semi-structured data models
Method: Designed SQL++ query compiler unifying JSON and relational data models
Key result: Proved declarative SQL can operate seamlessly over nested semi-structured models
Limitation / gap: Focused strictly on language syntax without physical storage engine optimizations

Title: Multi-Model Databases: A Systematic Survey
Problem addressed: Fragmented landscape of multi-model database systems and inconsistent taxonomies
Method: Systematic taxonomy of single-model vs multi-model architectures
Key result: Categorized multi-model architectures into extended relational vs native polyglot stores
Limitation / gap: Lacks empirical benchmarking under identical physical hardware constraints

Title: Benchmarking Multi-Model DBMSs: A Practical Perspective
Problem addressed: Lack of unified benchmarks for cross-model query processing and data transformation
Method: Proposed UniBench benchmark suite covering relational, graph, and JSON models
Key result: Demonstrated that relational engines incur significant join penalties on nested JSON
Limitation / gap: Did not isolate field-level update overheads or tail latency (p99) percentiles

Title: Adaptive Indexing for Semi-Structured JSON Documents in Relational Systems
Problem addressed: Excessive storage overhead and maintenance costs of exhaustive inverted JSON indexing
Method: Designed adaptive path-filtering index tree for relational JSON columns
Dataset: TPC-H adapted JSON and Twitter streaming datasets
Key result: Reduced index footprint by 45% while maintaining fast query selectivity
Limitation / gap: Requires continuous query workload profiling; non-standard PostgreSQL engine patch

Title: Multi-Model Transaction Management: Isolation and Scalability
Problem addressed: Cross-model transactional atomicity and multi-version concurrency control anomalies
Method: Formalized multi-model ACID protocols and multi-version concurrency isolation
Key result: Demonstrated that multi-model ACID incurs 35% throughput penalty vs single-model
Limitation / gap: Evaluated custom research prototype rather than enterprise-grade database engines

Title: Optimizing Schema-Agnostic JSON Storage in Relational Engines
Problem addressed: High storage footprint and serialization cost of binary JSON in relational tables
Method: Proposed columnar dictionary encoding for nested JSON attributes
Dataset: GitHub Archive and Yelp academic datasets
Key result: Achieved 2.8x compression ratio and 40% faster projection scans on analytical paths
Limitation / gap: Focuses strictly on analytical read paths; degrades write and update throughput by 22%

Title: Comprehensive Benchmarking of NoSQL and NewSQL Databases Under Mixed HTAP Workloads
Problem addressed: Ambiguity in database selection for hybrid transaction/analytical applications
Method: Empirical comparison of CockroachDB, MongoDB, and Apache Cassandra
Key result: Confirmed NewSQL matches NoSQL scalability while enforcing serializable ACID

Title: Document Stores vs. Relational JSON: A Comparative Architectural Study
Problem addressed: Performance gap between native document stores and relational JSONB engines
Method: In-depth empirical study of MongoDB, Couchbase, PostgreSQL, and MySQL
Key result: PostgreSQL JSONB competitive on point lookups; trailed native stores on bulk writes
Limitation / gap: Lacks tail-latency (p99) characterization under high-concurrency partial mutations

Title: High-Throughput Partial Update Strategies for Binary JSON Columns in RDBMS
Problem addressed: In-place update inefficiency and tuple duplication in decomposed binary JSON
Method: Implemented differential delta logging for PostgreSQL JSONB tuples
Dataset: High-frequency sensor and financial logging data
Key result: Eliminated full-tuple rewrite, improving update throughput by 3.2x
Limitation / gap: Evaluated custom research patch; not integrated into mainline PostgreSQL core

Title: B-Tree vs. LSM-Tree: Trade-offs in Modern Multi-Model Cloud Storage Engines
Problem addressed: Engine selection dilemmas under mixed read/write cloud workloads on NVMe storage
Method: Analytical modeling and empirical stress testing on cloud NVMe drives
Dataset: Cloud telemetry and IoT streaming traces
Key result: LSM-Trees provided 4x higher write throughput; B-Trees delivered 60% lower read latency
Limitation / gap: Did not evaluate in-memory systems or secondary index maintenance costs

Title: Quantifying PACELC Trade-Offs in Distributed Multi-Model Systems Under Partition Anomalies
Problem addressed: Lack of quantitative metrics for PACELC operational boundaries under cloud network jitter
Method: Fault injection and network jitter simulation across distributed multi-datacenter nodes
Key result: Mapped empirical latency frontiers across varying distributed replication quorums
Limitation / gap: Focused strictly on network latency, ignoring local disk page layout mechanics

Title: In-Memory Acceleration and SIMD Vectorization for Semi-Structured Document Data
Problem addressed: In-memory key-value bottlenecks when parsing serialized JSON strings
Method: Engineered native SIMD-accelerated JSON parser utilizing AVX-512 vectorization
Dataset: Micro-benchmarks on raw JSON string extraction in RAM
Key result: Demonstrated 8x speedup in JSON extraction utilizing AVX-512 vector instructions
Limitation / gap: Restricted to pure in-memory systems; leaves disk page storage unaddressed

Title: A Decade of NoSQL Convergence: Architectural Taxonomy, Unified Systems, and Open Challenges
Problem addressed: Lack of unified architectural synthesis after 15 years of NoSQL and multi-model evolution
Method: Longitudinal analysis of 40 commercial and open-source database engines
Dataset: Historical benchmark meta-analysis and architectural tracing
Key result: Formalized the convergence cycle: NoSQL absorbs transactions, RDBMS absorbs models
Limitation / gap: Broad qualitative survey without primary empirical benchmarking experiments
